gloss: A tiny part of a much larger whole.
teaser: Ever felt like your contribution was just a drop in the ocean? This idiom captures that perfectly.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever felt like your contribution was just a drop in the ocean? This idiom captures that perfectly. [break 1s] The phrase is: 九牛一毛, jiǔ niú yī máo. [break 1s] 九 (jiǔ) means 'nine' [break 0.5s] 牛 (niú) means 'cows' [break 0.5s] 一 (yī) means 'one' [break 0.5s] 毛 (máo) means 'hair' or 'fur' [break 0.5s]. Full idiom: 九牛一毛 literally translates to 'nine cows and one hair,' figuratively meaning a tiny part of a much larger whole. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a time when people noted how insignificant a single hair was in comparison to a herd of nine cows. It became a metaphor for something that is negligible compared to a larger context. The expression emphasizes how small individual contributions can seem against a vast backdrop. [break 1.5s] Example one: 这份工作对公司的发展来说，九牛一毛。 [break 1s] This job is just a tiny part of the company's development. [break 1s] Example two: 你捐的这点钱，对整个慈善项目来说，九牛一毛。 [break 1s] The amount you donated is just a drop in the bucket for the entire charity project. [break 1s] Example three: 他在团队里的努力，九牛一毛。 [break 1s] His efforts in the team are just a small contribution. [break 1s] So remember, 九牛一毛 means a tiny part of a much larger whole. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
